q: The tendency for catenation in the Group 14 elements is in the order
question: The tendency for catenation in the Group 14 elements is in the order
options: $\mathrm{C} \lll \mathrm{Si}<\mathrm{Ge} \lll \mathrm{Sn}$
$\mathrm{C} \ggg \mathrm{Si}>\mathrm{Ge} \ggg \mathrm{Sn}$
$\mathrm{C} \lll \mathrm{Si}<\mathrm{Ge} \simeq \mathrm{Sn}$
$\mathrm{C} \ggg \mathrm{Si}>\mathrm{Ge} \simeq \mathrm{Sn}$
solution:
Correct option: D — $\mathrm{C} \ggg \mathrm{Si} > \mathrm{Ge} \simeq \mathrm{Sn}$

Catenation means the ability of an element to link with atoms of its own kind and form long chains or rings. Whether an element can do this well depends mainly on the strength of the bond it forms with itself.

If we look at the bond enthalpy values going down Group 14:

$$\mathrm{C-C} \approx 348,\quad \mathrm{Si-Si} \approx 297,\quad \mathrm{Ge-Ge} \approx 260,\quad \mathrm{Sn-Sn} \approx 240 \ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Carbon has a very small size, so its orbitals overlap effectively and the C–C bond becomes very strong. This is why carbon forms an enormous number of chain compounds — the whole of organic chemistry rests on this property.

As we move down the group, the atomic size keeps increasing. Larger atoms cannot overlap their orbitals as efficiently, so the M–M bond becomes weaker and weaker. Silicon can still form fairly long chains (silanes), germanium forms only a few, tin forms hardly any, and lead shows practically no catenation because the Pb–Pb bond is too weak.

Notice also that the Ge–Ge and Sn–Sn bond strengths are quite close to each other, which is why their tendency is shown as nearly equal, $\mathrm{Ge} \simeq \mathrm{Sn}$.

So the decreasing order of catenation is carbon much greater than silicon, then germanium and tin nearly the same, which matches option D.

Statement 1 : Carbon monoxide can be estimated by using iodine pentoxide.

Statement 2 : Carbon monoxide is oxidized to $\mathrm{CO}_2$, due to oxidizing action of $\mathrm{I}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$ resulting in the formation of $\mathrm{I}_2$ which can be quantitatively titrated with hypo solution.
question:
Statement 1 : Carbon monoxide can be estimated by using iodine pentoxide.

Statement 2 : Carbon monoxide is oxidized to $\mathrm{CO}_2$, due to oxidizing action of $\mathrm{I}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$ resulting in the formation of $\mathrm{I}_2$ which can be quantitatively titrated with hypo solution.
options: Both the Statements are true and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1.
Both the Statements are true and Statement 2 is not the correct explanation of Statement 1.
Statement 1 is true and Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false and Statement 2 is true.
solution:
Carbon monoxide ($\mathrm{CO}$) is quantitatively estimated using iodine pentoxide ($\mathrm{I}_2\mathrm{O}_5$). This makes Statement 1 true.

In this method, when carbon monoxide is passed over warm iodine pentoxide, it gets oxidized to carbon dioxide ($\mathrm{CO}_2$), and $\mathrm{I}_2\mathrm{O}_5$ is reduced to elemental iodine ($\mathrm{I}_2$):

$$5\mathrm{CO} + $\mathrm{I}$_2\mathrm{O}_5 \rightarrow 5\mathrm{CO}_2 + $\mathrm{I}$_2$$

The iodine gas liberated in this reaction is collected and titrated against a standard sodium thiosulphate ($\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3$, also known as hypo) solution using starch as an indicator:

$$\mathrm{I}_2 + 2\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaI} + \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}_4\mathrm{O}_6$$

By knowing the amount of hypo solution consumed, we can find the amount of liberated iodine, which directly tells us the amount of carbon monoxide originally present.

Since this reaction sequence provides the exact working principle behind the estimation of $\mathrm{CO}$, Statement 2 is also true and correctly explains Statement 1.

Correct Option: Option A (Both the Statements are true and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1.)

question:

options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of the A.
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation of the A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
solution:
When stannous chloride ($\text{SnCl}_2$) is added to a solution of gold chloride ($\text{AuCl}_3$), a redox reaction takes place.

$\text{SnCl}_2$ acts as a reducing agent and reduces $\text{Au}^{3+}$ in $\text{AuCl}_3$ to metallic gold ($\text{Au}$):

$$2\text{AuCl}_3 + 3\text{SnCl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{Au} + 3\text{SnCl}_4$$

The gold formed in this reaction remains suspended as fine colloidal particles. This colloidal gold sol has an intense purple or ruby-red colour, commonly known as the Purple of Cassius.

Both the Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Correct Option: Option A

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Graphite is thermodynamically more stable than diamond.
Diamond is thermodynamically more stable than graphite.
Graphite has such a high thermodynamical stability that diamond spontaneously changes into graphite in ordinary conditions.
Graphite and diamond have equal thermodynamic stability.
solution:
Carbon exists in different allotropic forms, with graphite and diamond being two well-known crystalline forms.

Thermodynamic stability of a substance depends on its standard enthalpy of formation ($\Delta_f H^\circ$) and free energy.

By convention, the standard enthalpy of formation of graphite at $298.15\text{ K}$ and $1\text{ bar}$ pressure is taken as zero because it is the most stable allotrope of carbon under standard conditions:

$$\Delta_f H^\circ (\text{graphite}) = 0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

For diamond, the standard enthalpy of formation has a positive value:

$$\Delta_f H^\circ (\text{diamond}) = +1.90\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Since graphite has a lower enthalpy and lower standard Gibbs free energy than diamond, graphite is thermodynamically more stable than diamond.

Although graphite is more stable, diamond does not readily convert into graphite at room temperature. This is because the conversion process requires breaking strong covalent bonds in the rigid three-dimensional network of diamond, which requires a very large amount of activation energy. As a result, the conversion rate is practically zero under ordinary conditions.

Therefore, the correct statement is Option A.

question: Carbon and silicon belong to Group 4. The maximum coordination number of carbon in commonly occurring compounds is four whereas that of silicon is six. This is due to
options: larger size of silicon.
availability of d-orbitals in silicon.
silicon being vulnerable to attack by nucleophilic reagents.
more electropositive nature of silicon.
solution:
Carbon belongs to the second period of the periodic table, and its valence shell ($n=2$) contains only $s$ and $p$ orbitals. Due to the absence of vacant $d$-orbitals, carbon cannot expand its octet and is restricted to a maximum coordination number of four.

Silicon belongs to the third period and has vacant $3d$-orbitals available in its valence shell. Because of the availability of these empty $d$-orbitals, silicon can expand its octet to accommodate more than four pairs of electrons. This allows it to exhibit a maximum coordination number of six, such as in the $[SiF_6]^{2-}$ complex ion.

Correct Option: Option B

q: In the carbon family the elements other than carbon do not form pπ-pπ bonds because the atomic orbitals are too
question: In the carbon family the elements other than carbon do not form pπ-pπ bonds because the atomic orbitals are too
options: small and diffuse to undergo effective lateral overlap.
large and diffuse to undergo effective lateral overlap.
large and far, too less diffuse to overlap linearly.
small to overlap both laterally and linearly.
solution:
Carbon has a small atomic size, which allows its $2p$ orbitals to come close together and overlap sideways effectively, forming strong $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds.

As we move down the group from carbon to silicon, germanium, tin, and lead, the atomic size increases significantly. The valence $p$ orbitals (such as $3p$, $4p$, and so on) become much larger and more spread out (diffuse). Because of their large size and diffuse nature, these orbitals cannot approach each other closely enough to have effective lateral (sideways) overlap. As a result, the heavier elements of the carbon family do not readily form $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds.

Therefore, the correct choice is Option B: large and diffuse to undergo effective lateral overlap.

question: Stability of hydrides of carbon family.
options: CH$_4$ > SiH$_4$ > GeH$_4$ > SnH$_4$ > PbH$_4$
CH$_4$ < SiH$_4$ < GeH$_4$ < SnH$_4$ < PbH$_4$
CH$_4$ > SnH$_4$ > GeH$_4$ > SnH$_4$ > PbH$_4$
None of the above
solution:
The thermal stability of these hydrides depends on the $M-H$ bond dissociation enthalpy. As we move down the group from Carbon ($C$) to Lead ($Pb$):

  • The atomic size of the central atom ($M$) increases.

  • The $M-H$ bond length increases, which makes the orbital overlap less effective.

  • The $M-H$ bond dissociation enthalpy decreases steadily.

Because the bonds become progressively weaker and easier to break, the thermal stability of the hydrides decreases down the group.

The correct order of thermal stability is:

$$CH_4 > SiH_4 > GeH_4 > SnH_4 > PbH_4$$

Correct Option: Option A

question: Which of the following statements about the electrical conductivity of Group 14 elements is correct?
options: All Group 14 elements are good conductors of electricity.
Electrical conductivity decreases from carbon to lead.
Silicon and germanium are semiconductors.
Lead is a better conductor than carbon.
solution:
• Carbon is a non-metal. While its allotrope graphite is a good conductor due to mobile pi-electrons, diamond is a strict insulator.

  • Silicon and Germanium are metalloids. They possess electrical conductivity between that of conductors and insulators, making them classic semiconductors. Their conductivity increases with an increase in temperature, which is heavily utilized in modern electronics.

  • Tin and Lead are typical metals and are good conductors of electricity.

Because of this progression, not all elements in the group are good conductors, and the general trend of conductivity increases (rather than decreases) down the group as metallic character dominates. The most universally accurate and defining statement among the choices is that silicon and germanium are semiconductors.

Correct Option: Option C

q: The number of $\pi$-bonds present in the hydrolysis product of magnesium carbide is $\_\_\_\_$.
question: The number of $\pi$-bonds present in the hydrolysis product of magnesium carbide is $\_\_\_\_$.
solution:
Magnesium carbide is represented by the chemical formula $\text{Mg}_2\text{C}_3$. It contains the allylenide ion, $\text{C}_3^{4-}$.

When magnesium carbide reacts with water, it undergoes hydrolysis to form propyne (an alkyne) and magnesium hydroxide. The balanced chemical equation for this reaction is:

$$\text{Mg}_2\text{C}_3 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Mg(OH)}_2 + \text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$$

The main carbon-containing product is propyne, $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$.

Looking at the structure of propyne:

  • It has one carbon-carbon single bond ($\text{C}-\text{C}$), which is a $\sigma$-bond.

  • It has four carbon-hydrogen single bonds ($\text{C}-\text{H}$), all of which are $\sigma$-bonds.

  • It has one carbon-carbon triple bond ($\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$), which consists of one $\sigma$-bond and two $\pi$-bonds.

Thus, the total number of $\pi$-bonds present in the hydrolysis product is $2$.

$$\mathrm{Al}_4\mathrm{C}_3 + 12\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\mathrm{CH}_4$$

$$\mathrm{Mg}_2\mathrm{C}_3 + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Mg(OH)}_2 + \mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_4$$

Correct Answer: 2

q: A solid element (symbol $Y$ ) conducts electricity and forms two chlorides $\mathrm{YCl}_n$ (a colourless volatile liquid)$ and \mathrm{YCl}_{n-2}$ (a colourless solid). Name the group to which the element $Y$ is belong.
question: A solid element (symbol $Y$ ) conducts electricity and forms two chlorides $\mathrm{YCl}_n$ (a colourless volatile liquid)$ and \mathrm{YCl}_{n-2}$ (a colourless solid). Name the group to which the element $Y$ is belong.
solution:
The given element $Y$ conducts electricity and is a solid, indicating it is a metal (like Tin or Lead in Group 14). It forms two chlorides, $\mathrm{YCl}_n$ and $\mathrm{YCl}_{n-2}$, which correspond to the $+4$ and $+2$ oxidation states.
